Theme

Time, the calendar & feasts

monthly adjective and adverb

also every month, once a month, each month, per month, a month (per month)

classical

Cic. Att. 6.1.3: ūsūra (Lewis & Short)
Varr. L.L. 6.13: fēriās mēnstruās (Lewis & Short)
M-O s.v. monthly

mēnstruus, mēnstrua, mēnstruum

Declension on Wiktionary

monthly, happening every month; lasting a month

The adjective: monthly interest, a monthly holiday, the moon’s monthly course. As a noun, mēnstrua n. pl. are the menses (see period).

Other words

  • singulīs mēnsibus — every month

    phrase: ablative of time · also used · classical · Col. 11.1.21: bis singulīs mēnsibus, twice a month (Lewis & Short, s.v. recēnseō)

    The adverb “monthly”: singulīs mēnsibus, each month; in singulōs mēnsēs, for each month, per month, as in singulōs diēs (Dig. 36.2.12, Lewis & Short).

  • quot mēnsibus — every month

    also used · post-classical · Dig. 36.2.12 (Lewis & Short, s.v. quot); Traupman 311

    Formed like quotannīs, every year; the lawyers’ phrase.

Examples

  • tū cursū, dea, mēnstruō mētiēns iter annuum

    you, goddess, measuring out the year’s journey with your monthly courseCatull. 34.17–18

  • Singulīs mēnsibus ad avum īmus.

    We go to Grandpa’s every month.composed

See also month, salary, subscription, period.
